criteria.name: Distinctive Point of View
criteria.description: Does the design commit to a bold aesthetic direction (e.g., maximalist, retro, minimal) and avoid generic 'AI slop'?

scoring.1: Generic, overused patterns (Inter font, purple gradients, generic cards).
scoring.3: Attempts a theme but falls back to generic patterns in details.
scoring.5: Striking, memorable, and consistent with a clear conceptual direction.

criteria.name: Typography Execution
criteria.description: Are font choices intentional, distinct, and well-paired?

scoring.1: Default system fonts or ubiquitous choices (Arial, Inter, Roboto).
scoring.3: Acceptable but safe choices. Lacks typographic hierarchy.
scoring.5: Beautiful, unexpected, characterful font choices with strong hierarchy.

criteria.name: Spatial Composition & Motion
criteria.description: Does the layout use space creatively? Are interactions smooth and purposeful?

scoring.1: Cluttered or awkwardly spaced. No animations or jerky animations.
scoring.3: Standard grid layout. Basic hover states.
scoring.5: Unexpected/creative layouts (asymmetry, overlap). Well-orchestrated reveals and micro-interactions.

criteria.name: Code Quality & Production Readiness
criteria.description: Is the code functional, clean, and matching the aesthetic complexity?

scoring.1: Broken layout, syntax errors, or non-functional.
scoring.3: Works but uses messy inline styles or lacks responsive design.
scoring.5: Clean, production-grade HTML/CSS/JS or framework code. Fully responsive.
